publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: Photovoltaic System Design for Remote Telecommunication Installations
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Daily radiation records are used to optimally dimension array and battery sizes in stand-alone photovoltaic systems and to determine array orientation. The resulting system design has the specified power availability at minimum total cost.

articleTitle: A Modular 0.5 - 5 kW Inverter for UPS - Applications
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper discusses a realisation of a modular pulse width modulation (PWM) inverter with MOSFET-transistors, designed for UPS-applications. Each module contains a 500 Watt double-forward converter, equipped with a feedback circuit to minimize output distortion. Attention will be paid to the consequences of paralleling several modules: the load current has to be equally shared by the modules, defective modules must be removed from the system and the high packing density of modules requires a detailed thermal design.

articleTitle: A Remote Power-Feeding System with Converters Fed with Constant Current used for Optical Fiber Systems
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: For the first 140-Mbit/s optical waveguide link in the long-haul network of the Deutsche Bundespost a new power-feeding system has been developed. On part of the route linking Hamburg and Hanover, three intermediate regenerative repeater stations are housed in underground containers. They are remotely powered via their own power cable laid alongside the optical cable. Two series-connected power-feeding units per power-feeding circuit supply a constant current of 400 mA. At the regenerative repeater stations, converters convert this current into a constant voltage of nominally 60 V. As up to five regenerators can be connected to each route converter, up to 60 optical fiber systems can be supplied with power via the 24-wire power cable. The high power-feeding voltage (max. ±700 V) is only switched on after the feeding circuit has been automatically tested for continuity with a low voltage of 40 V and opposite polarity. Interruptions during service lead to immediate reduction of the high power-feeding voltage and indication of the faulted section. If the balance of the normally floating route is disturbed by a ground short, the power-feeding current is like-wise disconnected. Hazard to persons is thus precluded at all times. The line power converters fed with constant current on the route are a new combination of a step-up switching regulator (boost converter) and an uncontrolled forward converter. The constant input current is converted into a constant voltage, from which the isolated output voltage is then generated.

articleTitle: Two SMPS Integrated Circuits for Telecommunications Applications
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: Reliable Forced Air Cooling for Telecommunications Equipment
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Free convection cooled equipment racks used by British Telecommunications plc (BT) have an effective limit for system power dissipation density of approximately 2 W/litre. Power densities in excess of this which result from increased levels of system integration are most conveniently cooled by forced convection but the possible problems of reliability, maintenance, acoustic noise and capital cost must first be considered. Theoretical and practical work undertaken at British Telecom Research Labs (BTRL) has addressed these problems and a prototype rack has been designed and tested which allows power densities of up to 20 W/litre. This system utilizes independent fan modules used in parallel, together with replicated monitoring and alarm circuitry. Reliability calculations suggest a cooling system MTBF of 1200 years. Fan control electronics allows acceptable performance to be maintained at minimum battery voltage or when individual elements of the cooling system have failed. Optimised airflow design minimises acoustic noise and fan power requirement.

articleTitle: Computer-Aided Analysis of Regulated Switched Power Supplies with Unified Baseband Models for Continuous and Discontinuous Conduction Mode
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The conception of baseband modelling provides an efficient method for the computer-aided analysis of switched mode power supplies. The basic converter models derived by Cuk and Middlebrook enable the investigation of power supplies in time- and frequency-domain with closed loop as well as open loop configurations using a general purpose circuit analysis program, This paper deals with large signal baseband models for flyback and forward converters which - in addition - allow a unified treatment of both continuous and discontinuous conduction mode operation. The justification of the derived models is demonstrated by numerical comparison of the model's frequency response with closed form solutions for linear switched networks (implemented in a special purpose switched capacitor circuit analysis program). Results of comparable time domain simulations are presented which are based on the state space representation of periodically switched systems.

articleTitle: Cooling Requirements for Small Telephone Exchanges
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper reviews the principal cooling requirements and techniques for small, and very small, local telephone exchanges (SLE and VSLE). The requirements described are the `whole-life' requirements. These requirements comprise the cooling methods; costs; equipment; manpower; materials; data and time factors associated with the cooling systems throughout their useful life. The environmental reliability requirements are described along with active and passive means of achieving thermally robust cooling systems. In this paper a small exchange is one of 2000 lines or less.

articleTitle: Operational Experience in Connection with Renewable Energy Systems
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Renewable energy systems, especially stand-alone systems, have been studied, developed, and tested at Jutland Telephone since 1978. Computer-based supervision and control equipment for automatic or remote control of renewable energy plants as well as of conventional telecom power plants have also been developed and tested, and this paper will present a sum-up of the operational experience gained at Jutland Telephone in this connection.

articleTitle: Sealed Lead-Acid Batteries Operational Experience in a Telecommunication Service Application
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Sealed lead acid batteries have been under evaluation by British Telecom for the past 7 years. This evaluation has not been confined to the Laboratory, but has included significant product performance evaluation under actual service conditions both in the public switched telephone network (PSTN) and at customer based PABX installations. This paper will discuss important areas of operational experience in a telecommunications environment, and the manner in which some of the data has been used to suggest product improvements and provide users with a long term confidence in the use of this relatively new technology.

articleTitle: Asset Management of Power and Building Engineering Services Plant in British Telecom
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper discusses the introduction and use of a computer-based asset management system for power and building engineering services plant in British Telecom. Asset Management is a combination of engineering, management, and financial practices aimed at achieving an economic life-cycle, from specification through design, manufacture, installation, commissioning, operation, maintenance and disposal. for a specified performance. The system's primary purpose is the improvement of plant maintenance in the field and, from that, the acquisition and feedback of precise and comprehensive performance data for the interactive process of equipment development.

articleTitle: Technology Trends for Telecommunications Power in the United States
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the trends in telecommunication system power unit design and improvements to be incorporated into these designs in the future. The need for better power unit component materials and reliability, the advantages of increasing switching frequency and higher rates of forced-air cooling are discussed.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Systems for Remote Telecommunication Stations the CCITT / Gas 4 Approach (1)
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: - The GAS 4 Group was reestablished in 1980 by the Seventh Plenary Assembly of CCITT to rewrite the handbook "Primary sources of energy" (Chapter 1). - This contribution explains and comments the photovoltaic chapter of the new handbook to be published in 1985. It justifies the very low unavailability of 1,5. 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> specified for the telecommunication power plartstations (Chapter 2). - It describes the organization adopted for a photovoltaic system (PVS) to meet the availability requirement, and the operating principles of its components: photovoltaic modules, storage batteries, control units. It also gives a brief description of a hybrid PVS-FOG (fuel-operated generator) (Chapter 3) - The quality assurance specifications are emphasized (Chapter 4), as well as installation requirements (Chapter 5) and maintenance (Chapter 6). - Prices are analysed for mean or permanent powers between 50 W and 1000 W on a turnkey basis (Chapter 7). - To sum up, emphasis is put on the improvement brought by PVS's in telecommunication networks design, and on the close relation between rusticity and reliability.

articleTitle: Advanced Energy Management
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In recent years, the telecommunications industry has been in the forefront of technological advances. This has allowed the operating companies to offer their customers an ever increasing array of features. The power plant, however, has not seen much change in many years. In trying to design new systems, today's power engineer finds that he has two opposing criteria - reliability vs cost. He must sustain a high degree of reliability while contending with the increasing constraints of capital and operating expense. Adding to the problem is the continuous reduction in available manpower to operate and maintain the equipment. The engineer has come to realize that current digital control technology can offer a cost effective solution to his design challenge. With a properly designed microprocessor based telemetry system, better information can be maintained as to the current operating condition of the power equipment and any other energy consuming device in the facility. This, coupled with retained historical data and analytical methods, can provide the tools to make sound engineering or operating decisions. Or by taking it a step further, the information can be processed through algorithms and appropriate control action taken automatically.

articleTitle: On the Control of Magnetic Amplifier for High-Frequency DC-to-DC Converter
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Control characteristics of the half-wave magnetic amplifier for the high frequency dc-to-dc converter are analyzed. A new control method which removes a dead angle of the PWM output caused by the core characteristics and the reverse recovery of the diode in the converter is proposed. As the results, the wide regulation range is obtained for the high frequency, and the ferrite core is made possible to use for the magnetic amplifier.

articleTitle: Protection Techniques for Telecommunication Power Systems
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: NTT has been developing various techniques to protect telecommunications power supply systems against natural disasters, such as earthquakes, heavy rains, and lightning, because Japan is hit every year by such natural disasters. As a result of examinations in this area, NTT has intensified certain of its protection techniques in the area of earthquake-proofing, flood protection, and lightning protection. This paper outlines these protection techniques for telecommunication power supply systems.

articleTitle: Heat Measurement in Telecommunications Equipment Racks
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Medium and large local digital telephone exchanges have a typical power density of 230 W/sqm of gross floor area rising to 400 W/sqm in some areas of the exchange. Individual racks within an exchange may have heat dissipations equivalent to 1 or 2 kW or more. As future exchanges become physically smaller, rack consumption and power densities will increase. A number of thermal management options are available to the telecommunications equipment practice designer. In the U.K., current practice is to use natural convection, serial air flow rack designs but the use of paral1el air f1ow has significant advantages. In recent years, British Telecom and its major U.K. suppliers have conducted practical research into the thermal performance of equipment racks and have collaborated in the development of a new, parallel air flow rack practice. This paper reviews this work and illustrates how it has led to the production of thermal guidelines for rack designers and equipment planners.

articleTitle: "Safety Regulations for Stationary Batteries according to DIN/VDE 0510 Part 2"
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: DC Power Distribution and Grounding in the 5ESSTM Switch
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes the 48-volt dc power distribution system for the 5ESS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup> digital switching system. This distribution system includes duplicate feeder lines for increased system reliability. Each of the feeders serves half of the Power Control and Distribution Frame (PCDF). The PCDF incorporates fuses to protect the load from voltage transients and a capacitor to limit the transients generated during fuse clearing. The 5ESS switching system has a single point grounding system ("ground window"). This method of grounding is found to be the most ideal for controlling the external fault or lightning currents to which the switching system is exposed.

articleTitle: A Method to Determine Overload Safe Operating Area
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: When the load is suddenly shorted in a transistor circuit, the full D.C. rail voltage appears across the transistor and the current is limited by the gain. During this shorted load operation, the transistor is opetrating in the Forward Bias Safe Operating Region. The length of time a transistor can sustain this overload is dependent on the transistor junction temperature. This paper is a study of the variations of gain versus V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">CE</inf> voltage to 800 volts on a 1000 volt transistor. Also, the relationship of high voltage gain to the standard data sheet low voltage gain is investigated. Operation at high voltage and high current can result in excessive junction temperature which can cause immediate failures.. A method of determining safe operation based on the junction temperature just before a load short, using the high voltage gain and the Forward Biased Overload Safe Operating Area is presented.

articleTitle: A Stationary Battery for Diesel Engine Generator Starting
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In telecommunication plants high reliability is requested for the whole system and, consequently, for each component. Where digital equipment is employed, air conditioning is vital. Therefore it has become essential in the latest years a general use of Diesel Engine Generator (DEG) as standby power supply, not only for telecommunication equipment, but mainly for air conditioning systems. Due to the role of the DEG in the reliability of those plants, a dependable electric starting is requested. For this purpose SIP (Italian Operating Telephone Company) and FIAT S.p.A. have developed a new specially designed (ironclad) starter battery, able to supply high currents for very short periods and to withstand floating charge conditions for long time. Actually, standard SLI batteries, used up to day, have very good high, power performance, but very short expected life in floating service especially with occasional deep discharges, while special types with pasted positive plates and glass mat separators have shown a slightly longer life, but less power and, consequently, increased costs. The new developed type has a thin tubular positive plate fitted with an antimony free alloy spine, already tested and extensively applied by SIP, and narrow pitch between plates, leading to compact design. The paper reports mechanical and electrical performance of the new type of battery and results of extensive laboratory and field tests.

articleTitle: State-Plane Analysis of Quasi-Resonant Converters
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A comprehensive analysis of the high-frequency quasi-resonant buck converter is presented using the graphical state-plane technique. The analysis has revealed, for the first time, the presence of several unfamiliar modes of operation. The voltage conversion ratio and boundary switching frequency for each mode are derived. The existence of various operating modes are verified experimentally.

articleTitle: Thermal Management of Digital Switching Systems
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: Electrical and Functional Safety Requirements
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Information is given of a proposal for technical requirements of electrical and functional safety of equipment connected to the mains supply as well as to an administrations network. Such requirements have to be agreed upon in order to reduce the risks for hazardous voltage, current or frequency being transferred to the telecom network, there being able to cause human injury and equipment or operational disturbances. The requirements for a proposed safety barrier are discussed in terms of insulation and dielectric strength. Requirements for ground insulation are also discussed. Furthermore information is given how the proposal fits into the ongoing work of European and other bodies for harmonization of telecom network interfaces.

articleTitle: Experience with Renewable Power Sources for Radio Relay Networks
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes experience obtained with the renewable solar and wind power sources in remote areas as a supply for radio relay networks. The main point of the design was to achieve high reliability together with minimum maintenance. All selected components are of the highly reliable type, easy to handle during transport and installation and easy to operate. Much valuable experience has been gathered with largely prefabricated components, lightning and mechanical protection, energy losses due to dirt and supervision of the system. The main aspects will be discussed.

articleTitle: Trends in A.C. Power Conditioning for Telecommunications
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes the current characteristics of power quality and electrical and physical environment important for uninterruptible power conditioning equipment serving emerging telecommunications installations. It relates several new solutions using solid state conversion techniques to serve these needs. Characteristics such as electrical performance, power distribution, power consumption (real and reactive), input current distortion, load compatibility and interaction are explored. Physical characteristics such as size, weight, audible noise, heat dissipation, installability, serviceability and integration are discussed as well as ability to monitor operation locally and remotely. Solutions described include, 1) integrated uninterruptible a.c. power systems including battery, conversion and switching equipment as well as power distribution in a single package suitable for installation on computer room floor as typical of many new telecommunication sites; 2) combinations of sub-cyclic static automatic transfer switch and fast response continuous phase modulated SCR voltage regulators operating from a dual fed utility source to provide continuous conditioned power to serve a.c. operated telecommunications equipment; 3) the use of a load/line interface device with power conditioning capability for telecommunication's equipment reflecting high power factor and low distortion to the utility source, especially useful for single phase or limited capacity sources. Characteristics of these solutions are given and evaluated for use in modern telecommunication service.

articleTitle: Cooling System Ericool Experience After Five Years in Operation and Further Developments
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Since the development of electronic telecommunication systems started the heat concentration has increased from about 100W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and will continue to increase. A reliabLe cooling system is therefore essential for the performance of the switching equipment. Ericsson, as one of the largest suppliers of telecommunication equipment and services, took the consequences and decided to develop its own cooling system. It was the first and still is the only telecommunication company with an own-developed cooling system, ERICOOL. This paper describes first briefly the system and the design criterias. In the second part there will be feed-back from the field related to the design criterias. The further developments of the system and the different applications are described in the last part.

articleTitle: Experience with Hybrid Power Systems using Closed Cycle Vapor Turbogenerators
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: During the past six or seven years, telecommunications companies, P & T administrations and manufacturers of power supply equipment have shown great interest in the development of hybrid power systems which combine converters using renewable sources or random characteristics (wind and solar) with fuel operated generators. Among these hybrid systems, applications where Closed Cycle Vapor Turbogenerator is the back-up power source have been used widely where enhanced reliability is desired. This paper presents the experience accumulated over the past several years with this category of hybrid system.

articleTitle: New Ways for the Air Conditioning of Telecommunication Systems
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: For the air conditioning of high thermally loaded rooms, as usually exist in telecommunication centers, the air conditioning in general is characterized by a constant, all-year high cooling load and by a low necessary outside air rate. However, often certain room humidities have to be respected for operating reasons or for the comfort of the operating personnel. Simular requirements exist for data processing applications.

articleTitle: Some Consideration about the Practical Design of the Diesel Engine Generator in a Hybrid System as a Power Supply in Telecom Plants
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In this paper are considered parameters to be taken into account for a first approach design of a group thermal engine Diesel type coupled with an electrical generator. Some considerations are made about little electrogenerator groups due to the importance of their utilization in the photovoltaic and aeolian hybrid systems. So, tables are tentatively formulated with a practical character for a quick design of the systems. All calculations are made in view of a given use of the station battery by the optimization of its work, taking into account all the efficiences involved, in the case of power supply of telecom load operating in c.c. or c.a. modes.

articleTitle: Microcomputer-Controlled Charging and Monitoring of Batteries
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: Principle of Tracking of the Static Power Frequency Changers using Moments
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The paper considers some aspects of tracking of the output current standard of the Static Power Frequency Changers. The problem lies in the right choice of the one voltage phase of the network. Such a choice is based on prediction of the current of the loading. Discussed predicting control minimize the interval-by-integral quality index and the number of the commutations of the switching semiconductors. The paper also presents the properties of the moments and momentary transformation which facilitates such a control.

articleTitle: 30 Amp and 50 Amp Switchmode Rectifier Utilize Minimum Rack Space
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The paper presents advancements in thermal engineering and packaging for switchmode circuit design in a 30 Amp and 50 Amp 56 Volt DC (48 Volts Nominal) rectifier product group. The development has resulted in a design with excellent operating specifications and increased power density in a convection cooled communications rectifier. The design criteria are reviewed and details are presented for the rectifier performance specifications. The evaluation process which led to the concepts in structural topology is also discussed.

articleTitle: Microprocessor Application to NTT Power Plant
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Applying Microprocessors to the power plant produces many good effects, such as smaller size and lighter weight eqipment, easy maintenance, economy improvements. For these reasons, NTT is going forward with the introduction of microprocessors to its various power eqipment units and systems. This paper discusses the background of today's expanding use of microprocessors, basic application concept, examples of application to NTT power plant and future trends.

articleTitle: The Application of Bang-Bang Control for Converters of Uninteruptible AC Power Supply Systems
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: An Integrated Approach to the Thermal Management of an Exchange
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Unrelated specifications of the thermal environment of the exchange room and of equipment performance can lead to overspecification and unnecessary costs, or to underspecification and unreliability. An integrated approach is preferable. This paper outlines some of the work done by British Telecom and two System X suppliers, G.E.C. and Plessey, in a joint approach to the problem. Backed by a British Telecom test bed, it has resulted so far in design guides, a powerful rack temperature simulation package and cost effective experimental building blocks to measure temperatures of critical equipments before the cards, shelves and racks have been laid out.

articleTitle: Remote Power Feeding of ISDN-Terminals at the Basic Access
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In this paper some principles of power feeding are discussed. For power supply of digital telphone sets the use of a DC/DC converter is a reasonable solution. With the implementation of the DC/DC converter into the terminal some problems must be solved like noise problems, decoupling problems and stabilized operation. A realization of a DC/DC converter is shown which has a good efficiency with loads from 10 mW to 1W. The converter can be used for the S -interface as well as for the U-interface in PABX applications.

articleTitle: New Power Feed Techniques for the Submarine Optical Transmission System
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Highly efficient and small-sized power-feeder for a submarine optical transmission system (FS-400M) has been developed by NTT. This paper describes new developments incorporated into the existing power-feeder. A series resonant constant current converter, a common control method for stabilizing the output current of each converter, and a new load sharing method for equalizing the power-feeder output voltages are applied to the power-feeder. This paper also describes characteristics of the engineering model.

articleTitle: Optimum Power Supply Design for a Communications Processor
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: There can't be just one power supply for every application. For a special application however you can certainly reach an optimum. This paper shows how the design of an optimum power supply for the Siemens Transdata® communications processor also depends on the design of the entire computer.

articleTitle: Power Supply of Optical Subscriber Systems as Established in the Bigfon Trial System
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Although development of power supply of SCUs was not the main target of the BIGFON concept a number of important hints for further studies on subscriber connection systems is given. The solutions set up in the BIGFON trial show that it is possible to fulfill the requirements of integrated systems even at the present time. But it is also shown that in connection with the development of transmission technics further progress in the field of power supply systems can be reached. We are convinced that this is possible if the authorities give the right impulse that means ask for a big amount of such systems. Beside the demand of moving-picture-services a change of the used circuit technology from ECL to CMOS structures - down to the sub-u-region - also for high bitrates like 150 Mbit/s is essential. The number is figured out by the studies on ISDN-B carried out up to now. (1) Karl-Ernst Kneisel, BIGFON-Vergleich der verschiedenen Systemlösungen, ntz Bd. 36 (1983) Heft 7 (2) Klaus D. Frey, Klaus Prisille: BIGFON - Stromversorgungseinrichtungen, ANT Nachrichtentechnische Berichte, Heft 1, Mai 1984 (3) Günter Weinfurtner, Stromversorgung im Teilnehmergerät, TEKADE, BIGFON - Sonderheft 1984 (4) Helmut Bauch, Karl Weinhardt, Nachrichtenübertragung im Teilnehmerbereich optischer Breitbandnetze, Siemens telcom report 6 (1983) (5) Der Bundesminister für das Post- und Fernmeldewesen, Stab 202, Konzept der DBP zur Weiterentwicklung der Fernmeldeinfrastruktur, 1984

articleTitle: Telephoning using Light and Solar Energy
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: New telephone systems have been installed by the Deutsche Bundespost on lines vulnerable to lightning in the Bavarian mountains. Initially eleven mountain huts were linked to the valley by these communication links. Light plays an important parts in these installations in two different ways: The transmission paths are optical waveguides, and the power is supplied by solar cells. Now that this type of subscriber line has given excellent service for five years, the DBP is to set up further facilities on a large scale.

articleTitle: Uninterruptible Power Supply System (UPS) with PWM Inverter and Microprocessor Controlled Measuring Equipment
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes a single phase static UPS (uninterruptible power supply system) comprising of an inverter which uses high current transistors for a power range which was reserved to thyristors up to now. A microprocessor controlled measuring system calculates all data of interest such as input and output power, efficiency etc. The basic theory of the PWM inverter and the microprocessor unit is handled in detail.

articleTitle: Economical Considerations to the Layout of Uninterruptible Power Supply Systems
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: An increasing number of critical electrical consumers in industry and commerce must have interruption- free, high-quality power supplies. As a result, uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems have become increasingly important. Present applications cover the range of 500 VA to 500 kVA for individual units and by using parallel units, outputs of up to 2.5 MVA have already been reached. By provision of redundancy and also emergency power generators, an extensive series of modular system designs has been developed. In all cases, economy and operating availability are the prime considerations. The essential aspects of these considerations will be described for the various output series.

articleTitle: No-Break AC Power Supply for Telecom Application using Static Transistor Inverters in a Pulse-Width Control Mode
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: Basic DC Properties of a New Switch-Mode Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A new switch-mode power amplifier topology is proposed which features non-pulsating input and output currents and grounded load configuration. Basic static properties of the new structure are investigated anrd compared with the Ćuk push-pull amplifier. Optimization of the dc voltage gain linearity characteristic is performed. The influence of the switch voltage drops on power efficiency is examined.

articleTitle: Thermal Design and Simulation of In-Cabinet Electronic Equipment
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes thermal analysis techniques which can be applied to electronic equipment contained in any cabinet, especially those subject to natural environments. The method can effectively predict cabinet temperatures at various in-cabinet locations even when the cabinet contains fans and louvres to assist air circulation and ventilation. The technique involves a sophisticated analytical simulation using a proprietary computer software system (SCAMPER) but may also be approximated by a simple manual method using a scientific calculator. To demonstrate the application of these techniques, the paper discusses results obtained from a cabinet of telecommunications equipment consisting of: 1) electronic equipment, 2) sealed lead acid storage batteries, and 3) rectifiers to supply dc power. The results show the temperature computation at specific locations and the impact of the louvre positions. The battery temperature (internal and external) is also predicted which enables us to predict the expected battery life. In-cabinet environmental conditions, over a typical year, are also predicted.

articleTitle: Electrical Power Systems for Communications Satellites
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Satellite communication payloads such as IWT-transponders are highly sensitive against poor power source quality especially if they are operated on a common mainbus. Therefore the requirements on an electrical power system are stringent in terms of impedance, ripple and stability. General layout criteria are discussed for a regulated bus system (TV-SAT/TDF) and also for an unregulated bus system (DFS/KOPERNIKUS).

articleTitle: The Intellegent Power Room
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: Primary Sources of Energy - Diesel Generators for Remote Telecomms Systems
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A summary of the work on diesel engine generating systems that was carried out by CCITT-GAS4 in compiling the handbook on Primary Sources of Energy. The paper outlines the reliability requirements of diesel engine generating systems at remote locations and the various means of achieving that reliability. Particular emphasis is placed on environmental conditions, loads, plant selection and performance, quality control and testing packaged plants, redundancy, installation and maintenance. Additionally comparative reliability and costing of other prime energy sources are discussed.

articleTitle: Monitoring of Battery Operation Data in UPS Systems
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Storage batteries for computer feeding UPS systems are, in german engineering practice, predominantly rated for a shorttime performance lasting some 7-10 minutes. Given this high rate loading, we experience considerable variations in battery output coefficient with any load demand changes. UPS installations as a whole should therefore offer, under part load, a much prolonged bridging-over period than when supplying their nominal load. It is not however easy to assess such additional reserves in power, particularly not after a partial discharge. Hence the destinct expectation, on the part of UPS operators, of a reliable registration mode, i.e. by annunciator for the prevailing battery potential remaining to them in each case. The present paper outlines suitable designs for a battery status monitor, and the application of such a condition annunciator to diverse UPS configurations.

articleTitle: Progress and Trends on Primary and Secondary Lithium Batteries
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: Application, Rating and Performance Standards for Internal Combustion Engine Driven Generating Sets
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: There has been an appalling lack of performance standards which directly relate to electrical generating sets. Only those standards which exist for internal combustion engines such as ISO 3046 : 1977 are used and do not cover the criteria adequately. This paper is intended to provide some of the background to the development of an ISO standard for generating sets with particular reference to application, rating and performance.

articleTitle: Necessary Steps for the Application of Gate Turn-off Thyristors in Inverters for Uninterruptible Power Supply Systems
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Gate turn-off thyristors (GTOs) are more and more used in inverters for uninterruptible power supply systems (UPS). In the paper first of all the known advantages of the application of GTOs in UPS inverters are specified (losses, expenditure and noises). The paper considers in detail the special steps concerning dimensioning and protective measures that become necessary when using GTOs in UPS inverters. On the European market UPS systems have to be short-circuit-proof and have to deliver a high dynamic and static short-circuit current. This fact is the reason for the demand of high thyristor currents in proportion to the power of the equipment. The power range could be widened by parallel connection of GTOs. The results of respective investigations are represented.

articleTitle: Automatic Battery Monitoring System
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper discusses an Automatic Battery Monitoring System (ABMS) which provides sensing and monitoring capability to indicate the cell conditions in any number of standby power cells. The ABMS includes a Scanner/Display/Printer Module (SDPM) which is located remotely from the battery and transponder probes are installed in each battery cell. Capability is available to monitor any number of cells utilizing a frequency-shift-keyed signal to sequentially interrogate each individual cell and using modulated tone responses to transmit data back to the monitoring module. The system consists of a SDPM and individual transponder probes connected by a two-conductor signal bus. Depending on the probe configuration, up to five parameters can be measured at each cell and monitored at the SDPM. These cell parameters are voltage, temperature, electrolyte level, specific gravity. A panel display provides an LED cell-fault matrix that indicates when an out-of-tolerance condition exists. Specific parameter values may be displayed for any selected individual cell with the out-of-tolerance parameter identified. The built-in printer provides capability for hard copy cell parameters.

articleTitle: Agozn Batteries for Special use in Telecom. Equipment
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Silveroxide zinc batteries are used for telemetry and communication with satellites and spacecrafts. Referring to former and later space missions the silveroxide zinc technology, especially of rechargeable systems is described. Some recent improvements but also still existing problems are explained.

articleTitle: Diesel Powered Generating Sets in Modular Design
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: Boost Converters as a Means to Reduce Capital Costs
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In a telephone office, one of the main objectives is to maintain the load voltage above a minimum value for the required duration of a power outage. Often a mixture of old and new equipment with different minimum voltages complicates the situation. Also, the equipment is sometimes located far from the battery plant, resulting in large and costly distribution cable. In the past, end cell battery plants were utilized to solve this problem. However, reliability, maintenance, and performance problems discourage their use for new installations. This paper investigates alternate approaches to solving the problem by means of boost converters in new and existing plants. Like end cells, boost converters insert up to several volts in series with the distribution cable. Unlike end cells, the converters need not produce sudden changes in the load voltage. Also, the converters can be located outside the battery room. Therefore, the plant engineer can treat only those loads which require a boosted voltage. Equations are developed by the author which allow an evaluation of the capital cost savings possible with a converter plant. This is done by determining the optimum combination of battery plant and cable size, both with and without converters. The techniques are then expanded to include the costs of energy, money, and other related items. Sample cases are utilized to illustrate the use of these methods, and a computer program is included in the appendix to facilitate the use of the equations.

articleTitle: Magtronic Regulated Rectifier Inverter
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In magtronic regulated power conversion Systems a special transformer is used allowing current control of coupling between primary and secondary coil. This new regulator is competitive to SCR-regulation technique. Being comparable in size and control speed, magtrunic regulation features: Reliability, High Efficiency, Low EMF and Low cost. This paper describes the new control component and presents applications in rectifiers and inverters.

articleTitle: Power Supply Modules for PCB Mounting
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In the modern system architecture for communications technique, distributed power is going to gain more ground, since the technological innovation causes a kind of permanent change of the system configuration. Therefore, from the point of view of the system designer, printed board assembly with its own power supply module is the best way to meet this challenge. Some considerations show that higher costs of PSMs (power supply modules) can easily be compensated if the advantages, as for instant flexibility, maintainability and simplified power distribution, are taken into account. In the past, the miniaturisation of PSMs with professional standards was mostly based on hybride technology. Today, improved SMDs (surface mounted devices) combined with power MOS components are gradually competing with hybrids, due to their higher circuit design flexibility and comparable demand on volume. This paper is to describe our universal solution für PSMs, using SMDs and classic devices. Presented single and multiple output DC/DC-modules, suitable for EWSD and EMS requirements, offer a new approach to power supply configuration for communications systems.

articleTitle: Primary Sources of Energy for the Power Supply of Remote Telecommunication Systems
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: System Design for Small to Medium PABX Equipment
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Small to medium PABX systems are standardized in Germany according to their power characteristics with the designation "Baustufe 2". They are designed for between 30 and 180 extensions. On the one hand these systems are manufactured in relatively large quantities, on the other hand they are - due to the attractiveness of this market - under considerable cost pressure. The power supply is of great importance, not only in regard to the technology but above all in regard to the hardware cost. 10 - 15 % of the total cost is quite realistic for the power supply. Consequently the design of such a power supply is not only a technical problem but above all the problem of combining the best of the technical and economical features.

articleTitle: Batteries for Photovoltaic Power Systems
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper reviews recent trends in lead-acid battery design aimed at the long established applications, discusses their impact on the needs of the more recently emerged photovoltaic application, and describes a battery design specifically developed for photovoltaics.

articleTitle: Current Sharing and Redundantly Powered Voltage Buses
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Power systems employing redundantly powered voltage buses are found to have two advantages over those using dedicated stand-alone power units: high availability and more effective use of space. The reliability of the redundantly powered voltage bus is enhanced by output load-current sharing between the constituent converters. The degree of load sharing between paralleled power units affects system reliability, transient response and thermal profile. A control circuit that can regulate a power unit's output voltage by controlling its output current offers advantages over conventional pulse-width modulation circuits that control output voltage directly.

articleTitle: New Hybrid UPS-Systems, Preferably for Larger Power Output
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The hybrid UPS-systems have been developed by combining main elements of the so-called static UPS-systems with the synchronous motor drive preferably used in dynamic UPS-systems. Thus a system has been created which combines many advantages of both technologies. The advantage of dynamic UPS-systems in general and particularly at larger outputs is that no electric-chemical energy storage and - in many cases - no additional stand-by generating set is needed. At further rising outputs, however, kynetic energy storages - fly-wheels - have their economical and financial limits. Research work has been done with the aim to complete or replace the fly-wheel by hydro-static storages. The technical result as presented with this paper has been fully satisfying.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Reliability in Telecommunications
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: In order for photovoltaics to be a major alternative energy source we have to show people that it is a highly reliable source which can be used safely and reliably in high technical industries such as telecommunications.

articleTitle: Adapting the Basic Concepts of Power Supplies for Communication Systems to the Circuit Technologies used in these Systems
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The technologies in use in communication systems have undergone several radical changes since such systems were first introduced on a world-wide basis. By illustrating three stages in the development, this paper shows how these technological advances have affected system-specific power-supply design principles - particularly with respect to the system-specific operating-voltage requirements. The original communication systems employed analog modulators and amplifiers with thermionic tubes. These were gradually replaced by systems employing transistors. The last important development was the replacement of analog systems by digital systems. Each of these technological epochs: thermionic tubes, transistors and integrated circuits, the latter being the preferred type of circuitry for digital systems, placed special requirements on the system-specific power supply. This system-specific power supply - referred to simply as power supply in the following - is it-self fed from the installation supply voltage, which is normally a no-break supply. The power supply uses this supply voltage to generate the operating voltage required by the particular communication systems.

articleTitle: The Feeding Conception of the ISDN Basic Access
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: German Communications Satellite System Examination of the Necessity for an Uninterruptible Power Supply for Small Earth Stations
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: One of the main applications of the national communication satellite system "DFS-Kopernikus" of the Deutsche Bundespost, which is to start effective operations in 1988, will be the provision of business services. These "New Services" have high requirements with respect to service quality. The central equipment necessary for control and execution of operations in this sector will therefore be designed with redundancy and be equipped with uninterruptible power supplies (UPS). This examination determines the effects of mains power failures on the de-central small earth stations, which are installed in the customers vicinity, on the availability of the DFS connections. On the basis of the results, it was decided that the small earth stations of the DFS should be operated without UPS.

articleTitle: Developments in Classification of Electrical Equipment with Regard to Protection Against Electric Shock
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: An IEC working group has extended the conventional approach of specifying requirement for protection against electric shock to become better appliccable to electronic equipment. A draft revision of IEC Publication 536 displays requirements for a completed set of Classes. electric shock, protection, classification, IEC

articleTitle: Telecommunications Safety Standards in the UK
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: The Power Supply of Supplementary Equipment at the ISDN-Telephoneset
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: Solar Cell Power Supply System for Composite Overhead Ground Wire Telecommunications Systems with Optical Fibers
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes a solar cell power supply system designed for use with the optical repeaters used in ground wire telecommunications for ultra-high voltage overhead power transmission. Since it is difficult to assure commercial power availability for optical repeaters built near transmission towers, local power feeding is necessary. We considered the advantages and disadvantages of the following local power feeding methods finally adopting the solar cell system, it being generally superior in capacity, stability, ease of maintenance, safety, and cost. (1) Solar cell power supply (2) Wind energy power supply (3) Fuel cell power supply (4) Partial pressure in power line capacitors (5) Engine generator (6) Electrostatic induction in ground wires power supply The following items affect the solar cell power supply when it is installed at right under or near high-voltage power lines or transmission towers. (1) Electrostatic induction by power lines (2) Electromagnetic induction by ground-fault current (3) Lightning surge current flowing through transmission towers and ground wires After investigating these conditions, we decided that it was possible to implement the solar cell power supply system. We started verification tests in a 154 kV power transmission system in May 1985, and to date, have had no problems.

articleTitle: Progressive UPS-technology
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The technology of modern power electronics and with it static uninterruptible power supply - UPS, is now about 20 years old. Many problems were solved, for example good reliability and redundant and parallel systems became standard. But in the past UPS'es were expensive, bulky and noisy devices, they normally required special rooms for the units and batteries. The customers often had to make a critical evaluation if it was useful to install a UPS-system. Now this situation has changed based on 20 years of know-how and attractive new components became the key to a significant improvement in modern UPS. This paper tries to explain some examples of progressive UPS-technology and shows how easy it is to install and use modern UPS equipment.

articleTitle: Output Voltage Ripple in the Push-Pull DC-to-DC Converter
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The output voltage ripple in the push-pull dc-to-dc converter is discussed in this paper for the six modes of operation caused by the interaction between the magnetizing current of the transformer and that of the reactor. It is shown that, in the two modes of operation, both the low output voltage ripple and the stable dynamic characteristic of the first order are obtained even in the high load current region when large inductance of the reactor and small inductance of the transformer are used.

articleTitle: On the Parallel Operations of Triport UPS Systems
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Operations of parallel-connected Triport UPS systems are discussed. The parallel operation becomes important (1) for increasing the rated kVA of the system and (2) for realizing a redundant system to improve the system reliability. In this paper, we consider the typical parallel operation of two Triports under the normal mode and analyze the current balance conditions which make the ratio of output currents equal to that of the kVA ratings. Experimental results are shown about the current sharing characteristics at steady state, the output voltage transient characteristics for load current variation and so forth.

articleTitle: Multiple Output Switch Mode Power Supplies using Saturable Reactor Control
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: As the complexity of communications systems increases, so too do the demands made on the associated power supplies. This is true not only in relation to the stability of the output voltages within a wide load range, but also with regard to efficiency, volume and costs. The demands for high accuracy of different output voltages provided by a single power supply unit can only be met by direct control of each ouput circuit. Advances in the development of amorphous magnetic material mean that magnetic amplifiers can now be used as low-loss control device at the higher frequencies of 20 to 100 kHz, too. This circuit principle offers benefits in secondary regulator application compared with linear or switch mode semiconductor circuits.

articleTitle: The Use of Digital Switching Equipment in Buildings of the Deutsche Bundespost (Optimization of Cooling and Telecommunication Equipment Layout)
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: International Standards for Stationary Lead Acid Batteries
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A review is given of various national standards for stationary lead-acid batteries. The current situation on the first I.E.C. specification is given together with a summary of the problems encountered in its preparation. The I.E.C. approach to standardisation of New Lead-Acid Stationary batteries is reviewed, and a summary of work to date undertaken by the Working Group 3 (industrial Lead-Acid Batteries), on a new standard for large sealed stationary batteries is given. An opinion is given by the Authors on possible future developments in standards for stationary lead-acid batteries.

articleTitle: Battery Power Supply for Cordless Telecom Equipment
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: It is clear from our paper, that both types of NiCad batteries can be successfully used as the power supply for cordless telephones and other similar portable telecommunications equipment. The decision as to the particular type chosen, can be summarised as follows: Where dimensions and overall specification are critical, NiCad mass plate button cells should be specified. However, if the application should demand a recharge time of 1 hour or less, then sintered cells must be specified. FUTURE DEVELOPMENTS are in hand to enhance the performance of button cells in terms of extended overcharge capabilities, optimisation of capacity and to produce thinner section cells, this will enable the design engineer to make the best use of the versatility of this type of cell.

articleTitle: Methanol Fuel Cell Power Source
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Energy Research Corporation (ERC) has developed and delivered to the U.S. Army 3kW fuel cell generator sets which operate on diluted methanol fuel. To improve fuel logistics in terms of supply, weight and volume, ERC is also developing fuel cell power plants which run on neat (undiluted) methanol. Design of these generators is based on partial oxidation and internal water recovery concepts. With the water recovery concept, the dilute methanol fuel is obtained on-board by mixing neat methanol with water recovered from fuel cell and reformer exhaust streams. This scheme has been successfully demonstrated at ERC with a 3kW unit, using air-cooled commercial cross-flow heat exchangers. A 3kW power plant incorporating this design feature is under construction for the U.S. Army. ERC has also designed, constructed and tested a fully automatic 5kW neat-methanol power plant with water recovery from cathode and reformer flue exhaust for the U.S Air Force. This power plant has an overall thermal efficiency of 32% (based on LHV) at the rated 5kW load and is intended for remote baseload application.

articleTitle: Lithium-SO2 A Battery System for Telecom. Equipment
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: As example for the performance of the Lithium-Sulfurdioxide-System two possibilities of application concerning telecommunication will be presented. For application as CMOS-memory back-up the storage capability and run under weak load over a couple of years will be illustrated and safety aspects for use and handling will be pointed out. All data refer to the smallest cell type - 1/2 AA. Portable telecommunication equipment requires high energy density over a wide temperature range with maximum of safety. These qualities given by the Li-SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-system will be illustrated at the G2O cell (size D) and the costs of this system in comparison to traditional aqueous systems will be approximated.

articleTitle: AC Power Plant Modernisation in British Telecom
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: British Telecom has installed some 4,500 Standby Diesel Generator Sets in its telephone exchanges, radio, and repeater stations over the past 25 years. Given the changing pattern of equipment technology from analogue to digital systems, particularly in major centres, and the increasing penetration of AC operated computer based plant, a review has been completed of the power systems needed now and in the future. A study has also been undertaken of AC power and total system reliability. This paper outlines the areas of investigation and shows how enhanced plant reliability targets are being achieved, and maintenance problems reduced.

articleTitle: Microprocessor-Controlled Power Equipment
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: This paper describes a thyristor rectifier system controlled by microprocessor. We applied microprocessor to DC power supply in order to enhance maintenability. The following items are realized on development of the system: 1. Automatic charge capability, 2. Remote supervision and control capability, 3. Man-machine interface capability, 4. Running rectifier shift capability, 5. Self-diagnosis capability.

articleTitle: MOSFETs and Microprocessors Advances in Technology for Uninterruptible DC Plants
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Switched mode power supplies have substantial better technical qualities than conventional ones, microprocessor equipped measuring and monitoring devices are gathe ring more datas and give more informations At present both together are leading to a remarkable change of uninterruptible DC plants. With a special method the systems availability can be checked without dissturbing the normal operation.

articleTitle: Design criteria of brushless three-phase alternators for use according to telecommunication specifications
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: Economic Considerations for Reserve Telephone Power
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Considering alternate sources of power during commercial AC power failure, telephone engineers are faced with three common options: 1) A battery reserve normally ranging from three to eight hours of DC power. 2) A stand-by engine (usually a diesel engine or turbine) to provide AC power as substitute for commercial AC. 3) A combination of the first two options. Once reliability and office integrity criteria are satisfied, it is possible to vary the extent of options 1 and 2 to achieve the most cost effective combination without jeopardizing telephone service.

articleTitle: Diesel Generating Sets Control Cubicles
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Power supply of digital switching systems asks for a primary stand by power to mains. The stand by power is usually made of high reliability diesel generating systems, since the primary stand by power has to supply the air conditioning system of the telephone exchange rooms, essential for the exchange operation. In order to achieve high reliability levels, the performances of the control and supervision cubicle are the most important. SIP, the Italian Telephone Operating Company, has specified and ITALTEL has developped a new series of diesel generating sets control and supervision cubicles for power ratings up to 1000 KVA. Dimensions of the new cubicles are 600×600×2067 (mm) and each cubicle consists of: - electronic control, and supervision device - power circuit and ancillary circuits switching, breaking and protection device - battery charger - instruments. Highlighting features of the system are: - electronic overload protection of sincronous generators from 150 up to 1000 KVA - control and supervision device for all the diesel generating set functions, operating from the strater battery of the diesel engine and therefore with a DC voltage from 8V up to 30V DC - high diagnostic capacity for the diesel generating set - possibility of manual by-pass of the cubicle - interface for information management at higher level maintenance centres, through a processor system. The paper describes the features of the diesel generating set control cubicle, of the electronic control and supervision device and the results of tests and field operation.

articleTitle: Safety Requirements of Telecom Equipment; Present situation of the standardization Problems and possible solutions
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: With growing amount of telecom equipment exchanged by world trade the need for safety standards accepted all over the world is becoming urgent. Specific safety requirements have been set up by national telephone administrations and some national standardization bodies. The fields of telecom equipment, data-processing and office machines are growing together. For the last two fields international requirements exist. In a survey the structure and dependencies of the international bodies envolved in safety standardization are shown. The present situation of the work of the relevant committees is presented. Some problems specific to the telecom field are shown where applications of the international standards do not satisfy. Finally a way to gain solutions is named.

articleTitle: System Characteristics with Hybrid Power Modules as Embedded Power Supplies
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Already at the introduction of electronic telecommunication systems, embedded power supplies (also called in-frame power, rack power or dedicated power supplies) were an important part of the system design. Depending on the structure of the system and its subsystems, there were different requirements, on i.e. power, size, output voltages and number of outputs. Throughout the years, a wide range of DC/DC-converters, have therefore been used. RIFA AB recently introduced a new type of power supply, based on hybrid technique, where the traditional open-frame DC/DC-converter has been turned into an encapsulated standard component. This paper will describe the special features obtainable in a system, where these power modules are used as embedded power supplies. Emphasis will be put on a number och characteristics, which will give increased freedom of design. The following items will be especially discussed: reliability, efficiency, ambient temperature and power/volume ratio, as these are parameters on which great development efforts have been put into the power module. This paper will also give some aspects on designing small, extending or large systems, having the possibility to use the modules separate or in parallel or series connection.

articleTitle: Setting up, use and Maintenance of Solar Generator for Telephone Booth
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Telephone booth needs electrical power for lighting, payment card system, radio telephone. Connecting to a traditional network can be too expensive or not performant. The photovoltaic telephone booth is efficient. The system set up for a new or existant call box is easy, quick and simple. • Setting up 2 hours, 2 persons, no lifting material = assembly of the polyester roof on the call box + cabling of the lighting system + cabling of-the accumulators with fast connectors + tests • Use The use of the telephone equipment is identical to a standard call box The photovoltaic generator supplies : - either the light - or/and the card system - or/and the radio telephone The available energy is rated by the sun light and kept stock in sealed batteries. • Maintenance - cleaning of the modules when washing the call box - a test box is supplied to check the electronic functions The photovoltaic system has been studied with French PTT.

articleTitle: Verification of Computer Sizing of Photovoltaic Power Systems
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: There are no generally accepted computer sizing programs for stand-alone photovoltaic power systems, including the array and the battery, which have been verified for an extended period of time. In order to test the performance and the reliability of stand-alone photovoltaic power systems a computer sizing program for the solar array and battery has been developed. The program covers both vented low antimony and maintenance free lead-acid batteries as well as pocket plate nickel cadmium batteries. The sizing program has been verified in a one year full scale testing including four different types of batteries taking into consideration charge efficiency versus state of charge, aging, temperature, insulation, depth of discharge, type of load, catalytic vents and water consumption. The conclusion drawn from the test is that a pocketplate nickel cadmium battery with property balanced electrode capacity has extremely good charging efficiency in the actual current range. There has been no aging during the 12 months test and the retained capacity is better than for lead acid batteries. The so called maintenance free lead acid battery did not show satisfactory performance in this application.

articleTitle: Insulation Co-ordination in the Low Voltage Area
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Insulation Co-ordination means the adaptation of the properties of insulations - clearances, creepage distances, solid insulating material - to the operational and environmental conditions of electrical equipment and systems. The influences which can harm the insulation of telecommunication equipment are listed in accordance with the IEC Reports 664 and 664A. For classification of the environmental conditions in which telecommunication equipment shall operate safely and reliably, reference is made to the work of TC75. Furthermore the questions relating to type and routine testing of the equipment in respect of insulation co-ordination are touched upon.

articleTitle: A Fault Tolerant Power Converter System
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: A fault tolerant multiple outlet converter system has been developed at British Telecom Research Laboratories (BTRL). High reliability is obtained by the provision of multiple independent power sources with associated isolation/control circuitry for each power outlet. To achieve adequate reliability it is necessary to test the fault isolation components periodically to verify their correct operation. The system can shield the loads from commonly occurring faults such as failed (shorted or disconnected) power converters and short-circuit loads.

articleTitle: Influence of Electronic Data Protection Method on Power System Requirements
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: Stationary Lead Acid Batteries, Operational Conditions, Future Aspects
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Power System Design for Telecommunications
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Since its inception in the 1950's photovoltaic (pv) power has been consistently applied in the telecommunications industry first as a convenient power source for satellites and recently for remote terrestrial sites. The size of economically and technically feasible systems has increased from tens of watts in the early 1970's to today's largest commercial telecommunications systems of up to 1 kW continuous power. This paper illustrates specific examples of telecommunication power system design solutions in systems supplied by BP Solar Systems. PV module construction techniques and array design methods are examined with improvements in collected insolation and other environmental data. Battery sizing, charge control, protection and power system interfacing are highlighted, along with aspects of civil/structural design. The paper concludes that reliability will be the most important parameter in further acceptance of photovoltaic power for telecommunications.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility: Sources and levels of disturbances in the telecommunications environment
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: The electromagnetic environment in which telecommunications equipment has to operate may vary from favourable to very hostile, partly by reason of ambient conditions and partly because a considerable range and volume of disturbance is generated by the equipment itself. This Paper provides an overall review of the environment in both Administration and customer occupied buildings. It examines the controls and regulations currently existing and under discussion and studies the effects of hostile conditions upon the equipment. Some real-life cases will be described to demonstrate the points made and give engineers who may be unfamiliar with the subject an insight into its practicalities. Finally, the work of the IEC International Special Committee on Radio Interference (CISPR) and that of the Conference of European Posts and Telecommunications (CEPT) in the field of Electromagnetic Compatibility as it applies to telecommunications will be reviewed.

articleTitle: The Significance and Evaluation of Alternative Power Sources for Telecommunication Systems
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: During the latest 5 - 10 years of time as a result of the energy crises in the early 70:ies great interest has been focused on the development of alternative power sources all over the world. Both large scale alternative power systems and small scale systems for powering telecommunications equipment have been developed, tested and put into operation. The interest for small scale systems is not only initiated from the general energy point of view but mainly from the pronounced need and interest to develop rural communications in a broader sense. This includes powering single radiochannel systems, navigation aids and other industtrial communications systems at remote sites and offshore. The attraction of alternative power is the reduction of investment and operation cost in comparison to older technical systems. The paper summarizes todays trends and technical experiences from testing and operation, and give an evaluation of the market development significant for telecommunications. Some aspects and comments on the influence of the use of new inventions and technologies on the historical development in general and in the field of telecommunications in particular are also given.

articleTitle: Greetings from the General Chairman INTELEC '85, Ronald Dingeldey, President of the Fernmeldetechnisches Zentralamt (FTZ)
publicationTitle: INTELEC '85 - Seventh International Telecommunications Energy Conference
abstract: Presents the introductory welcome message from the conference proceedings.
